answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to one registered lotus pond in a real orchard. A horticultural registrar inspects each pond by lantern light on unannounced nights, when the lotus blooms, logging the visit in a public record; one registrar covers one pond per night, so inspections cannot be rushed or bulk-bought. The registration fee, paid in outside money, doubles for every further pond on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another real orchard lease, another pond, another night inspection, and twice the previous fee.
